passage: Researchers studying sleep patterns have found that short naps can significantly improve cognitive performance, even when taken during busy workdays. Unlike extended sleep, which involves multiple cycles of deep and rapid-eye-movement stages, a brief nap typically lasts between 10 and 20 minutes and focuses on restoring alertness. This duration is short enough to avoid sleep inertia, the grogginess people often feel after waking from deeper sleep. Companies in high-stress industries have begun adopting structured napping policies, recognizing that well-rested employees tend to make fewer mistakes and recover more quickly from fatigue. Although some critics argue that napping reduces productivity, most studies indicate that strategic rest periods increase efficiency over the course of a full work shift. As the science behind sleep becomes better understood, more workplaces may integrate short naps as a standard part of employee wellness programs.
